result.rationale: Line 13 interpolates the feed-supplied `url` directly into the HTML string `"#{url}"`. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\/\//`, which permits quotes, angle brackets, and script content after the scheme. The resulting post is created with `cook_method: Post.cook_methods[:raw_html]`, and `Post#cook` returns `raw` unmodified for that method, so no sanitization pipeline touches it; the embed view then renders it via `raw post.cooked`. Thus a malicious feed item URL like `http://x/' onclick='...` can inject arbitrary HTML/script. The mechanism is fully verifiable in t

adjudication.rationale: In `TopicEmbed.import`, it appends `"#{I18n.t('embed.imported_from', link: "#{url}")}"` to `contents` with the feed/remote-supplied `url` interpolated directly into an HTML attribute and text without escaping. The only validation is `url =~ /^https?\:\/\//`, which does not prevent quotes or other characters that can break out of the `href` attribute (e.g., `http://host/' onmouseover='...`). Since imported posts are created with `cook_method: :raw_html` and `Post#cook` returns `raw` directly, this HTML will be rendered unsanitized (e.g., via `raw post.cooked` in `embed/best.html.erb`), making this a verifiable XSS/injection risk from untrusted feed content.
